name: qip-brokers
purpose: Broker and exchange adapter framework standing between the OMS and a venue: a VenueAdapter trait extending the narrow Broker trait with session/logon, heartbeat, market data and book reconciliation, plus concrete simulated-venue, sandbox-DEX-model and REST order-entry implementations. Structurally excludes a live adapter — AdapterClass has only Simulated and Sandbox variants and rejects the string "live" at deserialisation.
key_contracts: struct VenueCredential, Secret (redacted Debug/Display, no Serialize/Deserialize) (src/credential.rs:276,214)
production_evidence: Imported by backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/gateway.rs:48-54 (VenueAdapter, ConnectionPhase, credential types, SimulatedExchange, RestOrderEntryAdapter) and backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/venue.rs:74-77, backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/feed.rs:64 — all compiled into the qip-edge-node binary's non-test code. Also imported by the qip-cli `demo --live` subcommand (backend/crates/apps/qip-cli/src/demo/mod.rs:90-94). NOT a dependency of qip-kernel (0 references; `grep -c qip_brokers backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src` = 0), so qip-api/qip-fastbrain/qip-deepbrain never reach it. qip-edge-node itself is never deployed: `execution_nodes = {}` in every environment tfvars (backend/../infrastructure/environments/{dev,stage,test,prod}/terraform.tfvars), so the code compiles into a binary that ships to no environment.
io_and_state: rest.rs opens blocking plaintext HTTP via qip_transport::HttpClient (src/rest.rs:184) with an explicit timeout; no TLS by design (needs the egress proxy per the data-and-streaming domain rule). connection.rs and matching.rs are pure in-memory state machines. credential.rs never persists a Secret (no Serialize/Deserialize). Timing uses std::time::Instant only inside a latency test helper (src/rest.rs:742).
status_reason: Well-tested (89 tests) and structurally paper-only, but the one binary that links it (qip-edge-node) is deployed nowhere per every environment's terraform.tfvars, so the code has no live process to run in.
gaps_observed: dex.rs deliberately does not implement VenueAdapter — no chain client, no transaction signer; only the pricing model half exists (src/dex.rs:56-61)
qip-edge-node (the only binary that constructs these adapters) is never deployed: execution_nodes = {} in dev/stage/test/prod terraform.tfvars

name: qip-capital
purpose: Central-plane counterpart to the edge cells: decides how much risk capital to allocate, issues the signed CapitalEnvelope grants cells trade against without asking permission, aggregates exposure across cells, computes margin/collateral, tracks per-user ledgers with tax lots and entitlements, and recalls capital. Overview module; see sub-records for ledger and collateral/exploration.
key_contracts: struct CapacityModel, CapacityBound (src/capacity.rs:85,31) — tests-only, see gaps
production_evidence: qip-kernel's Cargo.toml depends on qip-capital directly (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/Cargo.toml). CapitalAllocator/AllocationPlan used in central/plane.rs and central/regions.rs; EnvelopeIssuer constructed and used in central/plane.rs:36 and directly imported in qip-api/src/main.rs:1095 (`use qip_capital::MAXIMUM_ENVELOPE_VALIDITY`) and qip-cli demo (src/demo/mod.rs:95); MarginModel used in cross_margin.rs:82; RecallRegister used in central/plane.rs:40; CompoundingPolicy constructed in adaptive_cadence.rs:268 (Platform::policy_for).
io_and_state: No direct I/O (a service, no std::env; per the core-rust domain rule). State (ledgers, allocations, envelopes) is held in-memory structures composed by qip-kernel's Platform and persisted through the kernel's event log, not by this crate itself.
status_reason: Deeply wired into production and well-tested, but envelope.rs's own module doc names a structural cryptographic gap: HMAC-SHA-256 signing is symmetric, so any cell that can verify a grant can also mint one — inadequate for production, per the module's own documentation.
gaps_observed: envelope.rs signs with symmetric HMAC-SHA-256, not asymmetric signatures; no HSM/key-store, no key rotation, no per-envelope revocation, no replay scoping — named explicitly in the module doc as inadequate for production (src/envelope.rs:19-40)

capacity.rs (CapacityModel/CapacityBound/Capacity) has zero references in qip-kernel or any app — tests-only (grep for CapacityModel|CapacityBound|Capacity in backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src and backend/crates/apps/*/src returns nothing)

name: qip-capital::ledger
purpose: Per-user accounting inside qip-capital: mandates, eligibility, entitlements, cash balances, tax lots, pro-rata fill attribution across a strategy's book, and the mandate registry. The largest coherent sub-namespace in the crate (~4,500 lines across 10 files).
production_evidence: UserLedger used in kernel exploration.rs:91; EligibilityRegistry, ProductCatalogue and InvestmentRequest used directly in platform.rs (struct fields `products: ProductCatalogue`, `catalog`-adjacent state); MandateRegistry and Mandate used in kernel config.rs:11,18 for reading the configured mandate at composition-root time; Entitlement also referenced from qip-edge-node/src/venue.rs.
io_and_state: No direct I/O. Ledger state lives in-memory inside qip-kernel's Platform and is journaled through the kernel's own event log (not written here).
status_reason: Reached from every composition root that reads a mandate (config.rs) and from the exploration/allocation paths; the largest test file in the crate (tests/user_ledger.rs, 2183 lines) targets this sub-namespace specifically.

name: qip-capital::collateral+exploration
purpose: collateral.rs (1640 lines, the crate's single largest file) models the cross-venue collateral graph: which asset backs which obligation, under which margin regime, and what a forced close-out at one venue does to margin elsewhere via LiquidationCascade. exploration.rs (1255 lines) runs small-size probes into candidate strategies/venues and books their outcomes into an ExplorationBook, distinct from capital already allocated to proven strategies.
production_evidence: collateral.rs types (MarginRegime, CrossVenueLink, etc.) imported in kernel's asset_class_registry.rs:65 and cross_margin.rs:78-82. exploration.rs's ExplorationBook, Probe, ProbeKind are re-exported and used by kernel's own exploration.rs module (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/exploration.rs:60,90-92), which is the kernel's DISCOVER-stage wrapper around this crate's probe machinery.
io_and_state: No direct I/O. Both modules are pure in-memory data/decision structures composed by qip-kernel.

notable: (shared crate test count; exploration-specific: tests/exploration.rs, 285 lines)

status_reason: Both modules have direct, named production call sites in qip-kernel (cross_margin.rs, asset_class_registry.rs, exploration.rs) and dedicated test files.

name: qip-capital-fabric
purpose: Predictive capital fabric: forecasts where cash, collateral, FX funding and margin will be needed per region/currency/venue ahead of time, prices moving it (transfer.rs), knows settlement conventions (T+0/T+1/T+2), takes a pre-positioning decision against qip_capital's live limits (plan.rs), and scores the decision afterward (evaluate.rs). Overview module; see sub-records for the reached corridor/gate/journal control path and the unreached custody/destination/assessment path.
production_evidence: qip-kernel depends on qip-capital-fabric directly. DemandForecaster::new() and PrePositioningPlanner::new() are both constructed in Platform's own constructor (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs:4389,4489) and exercised by Platform::pre_position (platform.rs:18021), called each DECIDE-stage cycle per pre_positioning.rs's own module doc. TransferCostModel/FundingCurve/FxRates reached via the crate-root re-export used in platform.rs:96-99.
io_and_state: No direct I/O. FabricJournal (journal.rs) is an in-memory EventLog-backed state machine; qip-kernel resumes it from its own persisted event log (resume_fabric in platform.rs).
status_reason: The forecast/plan/evaluate pre-positioning loop is fully wired into every DECIDE cycle; the crate's own pre_positioning.rs module doc in qip-kernel states explicitly that a plan's moves never become transfer intents and 'nothing here reaches the fabric's gate' — see the gate/custody sub-record.
gaps_observed: "A plan's moves never become transfer intents, and nothing here reaches the fabric's gate. That is not a gap left for later" — backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/pre_positioning.rs:22-31, explaining that GateCommand's enforcement-point attestations are facts a human must establish out of band

name: qip-capital-fabric::gate+journal+tolerance
purpose: The seven-veto TransferGate (§37.3): CorridorAuthority, Caps, MinimumInterval, StatedPurpose, SourceBalance, VelocityAndAnomaly, KillSwitch, run in order with the first veto stopping the rest. FabricJournal::decide wraps every FabricCommand (wallet assemble/reconcile, corridor propose, gate assess) as an event-logged, replay-deterministic record. tolerance.rs holds per-venue-asset reconciliation tolerance schedules; wallet.rs reconciles observed vs. ledger holdings and raises drift/halt alerts.
key_contracts: struct TransferGate; fn assess(...) -> Result<Approved, Vetoed> (gate.rs:727,741)
production_evidence: FabricJournal::decide is called directly by qip-kernel's Platform (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs:7470,7601) for Wallet::Assemble/Reconcile commands the kernel constructs itself (platform.rs:7913,7922). The kernel also inspects `FabricCommand::Gate` when one arrives (platform.rs:7583, cross-checking gate.funding against Platform::corridor_funding) — meaning the Gate path is wired to run correctly IF invoked. But no production code anywhere (kernel or any app) constructs a `GateCommand` literal to submit: `grep -rn "GateCommand {" backend/crates/apps backend/crates/runtime --include=*.rs` matches only test files. So TransferGate::assess (and by extension the custody/destination checks it requires, see the next sub-record) is reachable but not exercised by any production caller.
io_and_state: No direct I/O; FabricJournal wraps an in-memory qip-events EventLog, resumed from qip-kernel's persisted log at startup (resume_fabric).
status_reason: Wallet-assemble/reconcile commands run in every DECIDE-adjacent cycle and are hardened; the seven-veto TransferGate itself is structurally wired (the kernel validates a Gate command's funding field when one shows up) but has no production emitter, matching pre_positioning.rs's own statement that nothing currently reaches the gate.
gaps_observed: No production construction site for GateCommand anywhere in backend/crates/apps or backend/crates/runtime outside tests/ directories
backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs:7583 shows the kernel is prepared to validate a Gate command's funding field, confirming the seam exists but is unused

name: qip-capital-fabric::custody+destination+assessment
purpose: custody.rs (1217 lines, the crate's largest file) models §37.4's three-enforcement-point agreement — custody class, custodian, enforcement points, attestations, and a TransferAuthority that proves three independent identities agreed. destination.rs is the venue-allowlist registry a corridor's destination must appear on. assessment.rs mints a content-digest AssessmentId (not an event id or chain-head) that binds an attestation to exactly what was assessed.
key_contracts: struct AssessmentId (content digest, not an event id) (assessment.rs:114)
production_evidence: grep for CustodyPolicy, TransferAuthority, EnforcementPoints, Agreement, DestinationRegistry, DestinationRecord and AssessmentId across backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src and backend/crates/apps/*/src (all non-test source) returns zero matches for every symbol. These types are required parameters of TransferGate::assess (gate.rs:741-753: `custody: &CustodyPolicy, authority: &TransferAuthority, registry: &DestinationRegistry`), and that function is only reachable through a GateCommand, which (per the gate/journal sub-record) no production code constructs. FabricState itself (journal.rs:529-535) holds a DestinationRegistry field but no CustodyPolicy/TransferAuthority field — those arrive only via the never-constructed GateCommand.
io_and_state: No direct I/O; pure in-memory policy/record types.

notable: (custody, destination and assessment are exercised in tests/corridor_and_gate.rs, tests/attestation_binding.rs and tests/custody_mirror.rs)

status_reason: Fully implemented and tested in isolation, but structurally unreachable from any deployable binary because the only entry point (GateCommand) is never constructed outside tests.
gaps_observed: Zero production references to CustodyPolicy/TransferAuthority/EnforcementPoints/Agreement/DestinationRegistry/DestinationRecord in backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src or backend/crates/apps/*/src

FabricState (journal.rs:529-535) carries a DestinationRegistry field but no CustodyPolicy or TransferAuthority field, so even the journal's own persisted state cannot supply a Gate assessment's required custody/authority arguments without an external caller

name: qip-execution-engine
purpose: ACT stage: the order management system (OMS), execution algorithms, multi-leg groups, a quoting module that structurally cannot become an order (no function converts a QuotePair to an Order), and origination gating for creating new markets under a hard-coded $250,000,000 (raw i128 units) maximum exposure ceiling.
key_contracts: struct OrderManager; fn submit refuses a live venue below live autonomy (oms.rs:371)
struct Order, Fill (order.rs:197,172); Fill::simulated set by the OMS, not the broker
production_evidence: Broker/Order/OrderType/Side used directly by qip-edge-node/src/gateway.rs:65-66; OrderManager and Broker used by qip-cli demo (src/demo/mod.rs:106-108); qip-kernel's Platform holds a SimulatedBroker/SimulationSettings/Broker (platform.rs:134), a QuotePair-producing quote_loop.rs (kernel/src/quote_loop.rs:88-89,213), a SessionRecorder (session_replay.rs:77) and reads feasibility (venue_review.rs:712). qip-api Cargo.toml also depends on it directly.
io_and_state: No direct network/file I/O in this crate itself; SimulatedBroker/LiveBroker model fills without a transport. qip_transport-based network I/O lives one layer down in qip-brokers (the venue adapters) and qip-mesh (the spine), not here.
status_reason: Deeply wired into both qip-edge-node and qip-kernel/Platform, 105 tests, and LiveBroker is a complete interface with no transport (reports itself unavailable rather than trading) — the crate's own doc comments call this out as deliberate.
gaps_observed: LiveBroker (broker.rs:641) has no credential, no FIX/REST client and no egress path by design — reports itself unavailable rather than submitting; this is the intended paper-trading boundary, not an unintentional stub

name: qip-risk-engine
purpose: The deterministic control function: autonomy level and kill switch (autonomy.rs), pre-trade order checks against risk state computed before the trade rather than after (pretrade.rs), and real-time book monitoring (monitor.rs). No model is consulted anywhere in this crate by design.
production_evidence: AutonomyLevel imported in qip-fastbrain/src/main.rs:46 and qip-deepbrain/src/main.rs:55 and qip-api/src/main.rs:34 (composition-root startup checks). OperatorIdentity::verified called 12 times in qip-api/src/routes.rs (e.g. lines 1404,1495,1579,...,2402) for every autonomy-change endpoint. PreTradeChecker used in qip-kernel platform.rs:183 and directly constructed by qip-cli demo (src/demo/mod.rs:129). KillSwitch::clear_global referenced from qip-api console.rs and qip-web console rendering.
io_and_state: No direct I/O. Autonomy state and kill-switch state are held by qip-kernel's Platform in memory and journaled through the kernel's event log.
status_reason: Reached from every composition root (qip-api, qip-fastbrain, qip-deepbrain, qip-cli) and from qip-kernel's Platform; no TODO/stub markers found; 41 tests including exact-boundary and dual-approver cases.

name: qip-portfolio-engine
purpose: DECIDE stage: PortfolioConstructor sizes approved hypotheses through the compute router into a Proposal (intent plus reasoning plus checks passed, explicitly not an order). Structural rules: a leg with no hypothesis fails validation; approval requires both risk and compliance sign-off; only an approved proposal can be released; a veto works from any pre-release state.
key_contracts: struct Proposal, ProposalLeg; enum ProposalStatus, Side (proposal.rs:131,44,73,21)
production_evidence: qip-kernel depends on qip-portfolio-engine directly (Cargo.toml). PortfolioConstructor::new(config.mandate, router) is called in Platform's constructor (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs:4514) and held as a field (`constructor: PortfolioConstructor`, platform.rs:232). ApprovedThesis and Proposal/ProposalStatus/Side are used throughout platform.rs (12000+ lines reference construction outcomes) and capacity_review.rs:74-403. Note: qip-api's Cargo.toml has no direct qip-portfolio-engine line — qip-api reaches it transitively only through qip-kernel; qip-api's own source only references it in doc comments (routes.rs:2742,2826, auth.rs:38).
io_and_state: No direct I/O. Construction/proposal state lives in Platform and is journaled through the kernel's event log.
status_reason: Directly instantiated in Platform's constructor and exercised every DECIDE cycle; 31 tests cover the dual-control and veto-from-any-state rules explicitly.

name: qip-lifecycle
purpose: Evidence and approval gates for the candidate→holdout→paper→shadow→pilot→scaled ladder (and retire, from anywhere). Gates never score (one failing check fails the gate); gates recompute evidence from raw series via qip-simulation-engine rather than trusting a submitted Sharpe; promotion to a capital-holding rung is unrepresentable without a dual Approval; demotion needs no approver at all.
key_contracts: trait Gate; struct HoldoutGate, PaperGate, ShadowGate, PilotGate, ScaledGate (gates.rs:52,130,490,629,744,871)
production_evidence: qip-kernel depends on qip-lifecycle directly and constructs/uses it in venue_measurement.rs, central/horizon.rs, central/foundry.rs, central/learning.rs, venue_admission.rs, central/factory.rs. HorizonReconciler has two real implementations composed in kernel: PoolReconciler and UnarmedHorizons (central/horizon.rs:439,581). qip-deepbrain also imports it directly: LifecycleLedger in succession.rs:68, evidence types in evolution.rs:50, HoldoutPolicy::default() in evolution.rs:194,3364.
io_and_state: No direct I/O. LifecycleLedger and TrialBook are in-memory; trials.rs notes a composition root supplies a durable store (LifecycleLedger::with_trial_book) — not this crate's own I/O.
status_reason: Gates, ledger, demotion and horizon reconciliation are all wired into qip-deepbrain and qip-kernel; but corridor.rs's own policy-computation function (`emit`, the thing that actually derives a CorridorPolicy from ledger state) has zero production callers.
gaps_observed: corridor::emit (corridor.rs:303), the function that computes CorridorPolicy/CorridorRuling from strategy standings, has no caller in backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src or backend/crates/apps/*/src — only CorridorSubject (a plain data record) is referenced there (central/factory.rs:28); CorridorPolicy and CorridorRuling by name have zero production references

name: qip-mesh
purpose: Two unrelated things sharing a name: (1) point-in-time data mesh ports (Lakehouse/Analytical/HotSeries/MasterData/Graph/Evidence, each with in-memory and file-backed adapters, no `latest()` method anywhere so every read carries an as-of) declared against the architecture's named managed GCP services; and (2) spine.rs, the central plane's half of the regional network mesh — CapitalDispatcher pushing signed envelopes down to cells, CellDeltaReceiver draining cell state deltas up, over qip_transport's durable spool/retry/dead-letter machinery.
key_contracts: trait Lakehouse, AnalyticalStore, HotSeries, MasterData, GraphStore, EvidenceStore (ports.rs:185,203,243,269,286,322)
production_evidence: catalog::Catalog is constructed in Platform (platform.rs:4450 `catalog: Catalog::new()`) and held as a field. spine::{CapitalDispatcher, CellDeltaReceiver, PolicyCourier, ...} are imported and used directly in qip-api/src/mesh.rs:74-76, gated by the QIP_MESH_CELLS environment variable (mesh.rs:88-90) — real production wiring in the qip-api binary. qip-cli's demo --live also constructs spine types (demo/mod.rs:124). HOWEVER the data-mesh ports (adapters.rs, ports.rs, provider.rs, backing.rs) have zero references anywhere in backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src or backend/crates/apps/*/src outside test files — grep confirms matches only in backend/crates/services/qip-mesh/tests/* and backend/crates/tests/qip-acceptance/tests/{compliance_proof,truth_loop}.rs.
io_and_state: backing.rs::FileBacking performs real file I/O (std::fs::read_to_string, create_dir_all, write-then-rename at backing.rs:71,79,98-99) for its dev/single-node JSON-file adapter. spine.rs uses qip_transport's durable spool (file-backed) for undelivered capital envelopes. No managed-GCP-backed MeshTarget variant is implemented; MeshProvider returns qip_core::Error::Unavailable naming the missing credential/project for BigQuery/Bigtable/Spanner/etc.
status_reason: The network-mesh half (spine/delta, catalog) is live in qip-api's production route, env-gated; the data-mesh half (the six port traits and their adapters, which are most of the crate's doc-comment purpose) is implemented and tested but never constructed by any composition root.
gaps_observed: MeshLakehouse/MeshAnalytics/MeshHotSeries/MeshMasterData/MeshGraph/MeshEvidence (adapters.rs) and the six port traits (ports.rs) have zero production references in qip-kernel or any app — data-mesh reads/writes are exercised only in this crate's own tests and in qip-acceptance

MeshProvider (provider.rs) declares BigLakeIceberg/BigQuery/Bigtable/Spanner/SpannerGraph/CloudStorageWorm targets but every one returns Error::Unavailable naming a missing credential — no managed-GCP implementation exists in-tree (provider.rs:1-17)
